name: אינטגרל מסוים של 1/(4−t²)^(3/2) – הצבה t=2sin(z) (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Find

\[ \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} \]

by letting \({{CT:3}}=2\sin(z)\).

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Find an antiderivative with the substitution, then evaluate it at the two limits and subtract.
Step 1 — The substitution and an antiderivative

We want to solve

\[ \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} \]

using the substitution \({{CT:3}} = 2\sin(z)\). So, if \({{CT:3}} = 2\sin(z)\) then \(d{{CT:3}} = 2\cos(z)dz\) and

\[ \begin{aligned} \int{{CT:2}}d{{CT:3}} &= \int \frac{1}{[4-(2\sin(z))^2]^{3/2}}2\cos(z)dz \\ &= \int \frac{2\cos(z)dz}{[4-4\sin^2(z)]^{3/2}} \\&= \int \frac{2\cos(z)dz}{[4(1-\sin^2(z))]^{3/2}} \\ &= \int \frac{2\cos(z)dz}{4^{3/2}[1-\sin^2(z)]^{3/2}} \\ &= \int \frac{\cos(z)dz}{4[\cos^2(z)]^{3/2}} \\ &= \int \frac{\cos(z)dz}{4\cos^3(z)} \\ &= \int \frac{dz}{4\cos^2(z)} \\ &= \frac{1}{4}\int \sec^2(z)dz \\ &= \frac{\tan(z)}{4} +c \\ &= \frac{1}{4}\tan\left[\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)\right]+c \end{aligned} \]

Step 2 — The definite integral

We need

\[ \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} \]

so, recall that if \(\int f(x) dx = F(x)+c\) then \(\int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b).\) Thus, define

\[ F({{CT:3}}) = {{CT:4}} \]

Then,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &= F({{CT:0}}) - F({{CT:1}}) \\ &= {{CT:5}} -\left({{CT:6}}\right) \\ &= {{CT:7}} \end{aligned} \]
